name: Per-command security choke point (ensureCommandAllowed)
what: Every agent command that touches a page is vetted against the tab's current URL before it runs, and navigation targets are vetted before the tab moves; only a short list of lifecycle commands is exempt.
how: Class Qp in browser-service.mjs wraps every command via runCommand -> ensureCommandAllowed. WV() classifies a command as none | targetUrl (navigate_tab_url) | currentTab. Exempt set (qV): browser_user_claim_tab, browser_user_get_tab_context, browser_user_open_tabs, close_tab, create_tab, get_tab, list_tabs, mark_tab, name_session, playwright_wait_for_timeout, selected_tab. History reads take a separate path. For currentTab commands the tab URL is re-read from the tab list, then ensureUrlOriginAllowed = ensureUrlPolicyAllowed (host assertBrowserUrlAllowed hook, scheme policy, site-status) followed by ensureOriginConsentAllowed (enterprise policy, persisted denials, consent prompt). Reads such as screenshots and AX snapshots are gated too, so a redirect to a new origin triggers consent on the next read.
verevonRelevance: Quarry already re-checks domains before and after each step; formalising one ordered gate chain (scheme, reputation, enterprise, persisted denial, grant) with typed outcomes would give BrowserBroker and Quarry a single contract.
notes: Line numbers refer to the beautified copy; the original is minified. The gate re-reads the URL after any approval wait (see the WebMCP TOCTOU re-check).

name: Typed denial taxonomy with decisionSource and retryable flag
what: Policy refusals carry a machine-readable reason, who decided (approval, browser, enterprise, guardian, saved user setting, site_status, user decision) and whether a retry is sensible; the model-facing text differs for retryable and non-retryable cases.
how: Catalog wS in browser-service.mjs defines 16 reasons (approval_cancelled, approval_failed_closed, approval_unavailable, browser_capability_blocked, browser_capability_unavailable, browser_context_unavailable, browser_navigation_blocked, enterprise_policy_blocked, enterprise_policy_unavailable, guardian_denied, guardian_timed_out, navigation_url_policy_blocked, persisted_user_denied, site_status_blocked, site_status_unavailable, user_declined), each {decisionSource, message, retryable}. Class dt (BrowserUseSecurityError) exposes decisionSource, reason, retryable. K4() formats retryable denials as 'check unavailable ... may retry' and non-retryable ones through Co().
verevonRelevance: Adding decisionSource + retryable to Quarry's 'policy denials' in BrowserObservation lets the Model Plane planner tell a user decline from an enterprise block or a reputation block and avoid pointless retries.
notes: The guardian_timed_out message explicitly says it is not a determination that the action was unsafe and may be retried once.

name: Anti-circumvention instruction appended to denials
what: Every security denial returned to the model ends with an instruction not to reach the same outcome through workarounds, raw CDP, other browser surfaces or policy circumvention; only a materially safer alternative or a stop is allowed.
how: String constants H4 (prefix), z4 (suffix), V4 (check-unavailable prefix) and G4 (retry caveat) in browser-service.mjs; Co(text) concatenates prefix + reason + suffix; K4() routes retryable cases to V4 + G4.
verevonRelevance: Quarry denials surfaced to the planner are plain strings today; a standard anti-workaround suffix is cheap prompt-injection and jailbreak hygiene for model-visible error text.
notes: Effective only as far as the model complies; it is a prompt-level control layered on the hard gates, not a substitute.

name: Per-origin consent prompt with scoped persistence
what: First access to a new origin asks the user 'Allow <browser> to access <origin>?'; the answer can be remembered for the turn, the conversation or globally, subject to org policy.
how: $R() loops: getOriginPermission -> approve | deny | prompt. WR() raises an MCP elicitation with meta {codex_approval_kind:'mcp_tool_call', codex_sensitive_action:true, connector_id:'browser-use', persist:'always' only when persistent approvals are allowed, tool_name access_browser_origin...}. handleOriginPromptResult -> D0/YQ writes the decision at conversation or global scope via the preferences store; accessApprovalLifetime can pin approvals to the turn.
verevonRelevance: BrowserBroker grants are domain lists; adding grant scopes (turn, conversation, persistent) and an org-controlled 'persistence allowed' switch would map cleanly to Application Plane approval UX.
notes: Prompt transport is MCP elicitation, so any MCP-capable host can render it.

name: Deny-first permission resolution order
what: Saved denials and enterprise denials always beat cached or saved approvals; approvals are resolved from the narrowest scope (turn) up to global.
how: maybeAutoAnswerBrowserUseRequest (class ha) returns, in order: conversation-level persisted deny; global persisted deny; enterprise network-policy deny; v1 turn cache; v2 guardian-origin cache (conversation scope); browser-use-turn-cache (turn); conversation persisted allow (only when accessApprovalLifetime='thread'); global persisted allow; global never_ask when persistent approval is allowed; otherwise null which triggers the prompt.
verevonRelevance: Document a deny-first precedence ladder for Verevon grants so Space or org rules can never be overridden by a cached approval (matches the 'Space access never widens owner-plane ACL' rule).

name: Enterprise per-origin policy with deny-wins merge
what: Admins can set per-origin policy for access, uploads, downloads, raw CDP, auto-review and persistent approvals; denial from either admin requirements or user config wins, and denying access denies everything else for that origin.
how: aN()/iN()/dN() merge requirements.browserUse.origins (+defaultOriginPolicy) with config.browser_use.origins; per field the result is 'deny' if either source says deny; if access==='deny' then uploads, downloads, fullCdpAccess and autoReview are forced to deny. Fields: access, uploads, downloads, fullCdpAccess, autoReview, persistentApproval, accessApprovalLifetime. OQ()/cN() also fold the generic network permission profile (domains allow/deny, managedAllowedDomainsOnly) into browser access decisions with permissionSource 'codex-network-policy'.
verevonRelevance: Quarry/BrowserBroker could expose the same per-origin capability matrix (access/upload/download/raw-eval) so org admins govern web actions per domain rather than only allowlisting hosts.
notes: The same network domain policy applies to sandboxed shell commands and to the browser, giving one egress policy surface.

name: Origin pattern language with apex and subdomain wildcards
what: Allow/deny rules use exact hosts, '*.example.com' (subdomains only) or '**.example.com' (apex plus subdomains), with IPv6 and trailing-dot normalisation.
how: eC()/tC()/rj()/Vc()/Vg() canonicalise a pattern into {kind: exact | subdomains-only | apex-and-subdomains, hostnamePattern}; QS/zg compare hostnames; IPv6 brackets and zone ids are handled; a lone '*' means all. Wg()/tj() implement glob matching with backslash escaping for URL-style entries. The WebMCP resolver returns allowed | site-denied | default-denied | invalid-origin.
verevonRelevance: Use the same three-form pattern syntax (exact, *., **.) for BrowserBroker allowed_domains so subdomain semantics are explicit instead of implied.

name: Guardian auto-review of origin access ('Approve for me')
what: Instead of asking the user, an independent reviewer model can approve or deny first-time origin access; approvals are cached briefly per thread and origin and can be revoked.
how: Two modes: guardianMode v1 (per-session single-origin 5-minute turn cache, Vu map) and v2 (Zt cache keyed {threadId, origin}, expiresAt = now + 300000 ms, cleanup timer every 5 min, unref'd). Zt.start() coalesces concurrent reviews into one shared pending promise; Zt.revoke() marks a pending review revoked; $R re-validates the cache after each decision and loops (continue) if the approval changed mid-flight, which closes a check-then-use race. Prompt meta carries codex_request_type 'approval_request' unless auto-review is disabled per user, per origin (autoReview deny) or by enterprise (disableAutoReview). Reviewer identity is read back from _meta.approvals_reviewer (user vs reviewer). Core config enum ApprovalsReviewer {user, auto_review, guardian_subagent}; UI strings 'Ask for approval' / 'Approve for me'.
verevonRelevance: Fits the Model Plane (approval authority stays there): a guardian reviewer sub-agent with a short-lived per-(thread, origin) approval cache is a pattern Verevon can add in execution-core without giving Quarry decision authority.
notes: The reviewer prompt text itself is server-side and not in the install; only metadata and config are visible.

name: Guardian v2 reviewer configuration and transcript budgeting
what: The auto-review reviewer is a configurable sub-agent that sees a bounded slice of the conversation (messages, tool calls, outputs, reasoning, even node_repl screenshots) and scores risk against a threshold.
how: Rust core config struct GuardianV2ConfigToml: async_classifier_mode, async_classifier_conversation_token_limit, free_guardian, thread_context, persist_scores, classifier_instructions, review_threshold, max_tool_call_lag, reasoning_effort, max_action_tokens, max_classifier_instruction_tokens, reuse_parent_compaction, max_parent_compaction_tokens, review_scope, transcript{sources: tool_calls|tool_outputs|reasoning, include_images, max_message_entry_tokens, max_tool_entry_tokens, max_message_transcript_tokens, max_tool_transcript_tokens, max_recent_non_user_entries}. Related feature flags: guardian_enhanced_node_repl_transcripts, guardian_node_repl_transcript_images, guardian_root_handoff_context. Risk levels include 'critical'. Events GuardianAssessment and GuardianWarning; otel option log_guardian_assessments.
verevonRelevance: Gives a concrete schema for a Verevon 'approval reviewer' agent: token-capped transcript sources, optional image evidence, threshold and lag limits, and persisted scores for audit.
notes: Binary string table of codex.exe; field semantics are inferred from names (INF) while presence is observed. Line numbers are in the extracted strings file, not the exe.

name: Strict auto-review for every WebMCP tool invocation
what: Each call to a page-defined WebMCP tool is sent to the reviewer with the tool name, description, input arguments, tool origin and a sanitised page URL, even when the origin is already approved.
how: ek() builds an elicitation with codex_strict_auto_review:true, codex_sensitive_action:true, tool_name 'webmcp:<host>:<tool>', tool_title, tool_description, tool_params = input (must be JSON-serialisable via Yy), origin = tool origin and page_url = MV(url) which strips credentials, query and hash. listTools is allowed without review; invoke requires the tool origin to be resolvable, and the tab URL is re-read after the wait: if it changed the call fails with browser_context_unavailable.
verevonRelevance: When Verevon exposes site tools or MCP-style actions to the agent, review each call with arguments and destination, and re-check page identity after the approval wait.
notes: Docs also tell the model that tool instructions cannot grant authorization.

name: Automated safety precheck for credential prompts
what: Before the user is shown a secure sign-in prompt, a reviewer checks that the prompt truthfully describes the form and that the credential recipient is trustworthy for the intended service.
how: sk() (automated-safety-precheck) raises a strict auto-review elicitation named automated_safety_precheck.<tool>. The reviewer rubric (browserAuthSafetyPrecheck.md) compares top_level_origin, credential_frame_origin, form_submission_origin, credential_field_metadata, action_targets and visible_page_content; treats branding and labels as untrusted; requires cross_origin_iframe.origin to equal credential_frame_origin; allows genuine login subdomains, SSO, passkeys, MFA/OTP; denies deceptive, malicious or uncertain flows. Failure modes map to guardian_denied, guardian_timed_out, approval_unavailable, approval_failed_closed.
verevonRelevance: A phishing-aware reviewer step before any credential handoff is directly reusable for Verevon's missing credential-vault flow; the three-origin comparison is the key idea.

name: Fail-closed approval semantics
what: If an approval cannot be obtained (no elicitation channel, cancelled, timeout, reviewer unavailable) the action is blocked and the model is told no explicit denial was made.
how: Wt() wraps createElicitation lookups and raises Oe({check, reason:'approval_unavailable'|'approval_failed_closed'|'approval_cancelled'}) with messages such as 'Browser Use is failing closed; no explicit denial was made'. In gaas-browser-environment mode the strict auto-review path stops 'before creating a user prompt or action' (Rs()) when review is unsupported.
verevonRelevance: Keep Quarry approvals fail-closed with distinct 'could not ask' vs 'was denied' reasons.

name: Security modes (default, local testing, GaaS)
what: The same runtime can run in three postures: normal desktop, a local-testing mode that bypasses URL and site-status checks, and an autonomous cloud environment where only low-risk reads skip consent and everything else needs auto-review.
how: LR table: '' = no bypass; 'disabled-for-local-testing' bypasses check-navigation-url-policy, check-url-site-status, origin/download/upload/CDP/webmcp checks (sets PV, AV); 'gaas-browser-environment' bypasses nothing and only browser-history-read, file-download, page-asset-cross-origin-fetch and page-asset-download need no user consent (IV). Selected by env var (constant To) and BROWSER_USE_AUTOMATED_SAFETY_PRECHECKS_ENABLED. Bypasses are audited with permissionSource 'security-mode'. The native computer-use helper forwards the mode in header x-codex-browser-use-security-mode.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same distinction between dev bypass and governed production; make bypasses explicit, audited and impossible to enable from model-supplied input.
notes: GaaS expansion is not stated in the package; INF: a hosted agent environment.

name: Server-side site-status (URL reputation) gate
what: Before touching a site, the client asks an OpenAI endpoint whether browsing agents are permitted there; blocked sites are refused without any user prompt.
how: Zy.throwIfBlocksUrl -> xS() builds GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/aura/site_status?site_url=<origin+path>&url_request_source=codex_browser_use[:backend]&conversation_id&turn_id; response feature_status.agent===true means blocked (vS/X4). Cache key is hostname without 'www.', TTL 24 h (NV=1440*60*1000), in-flight requests are de-duplicated. localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 are exempt. A fetch failure inside this path is swallowed (catch{return}) so the gate fails open even though the reason catalog defines site_status_unavailable. The native computer-use helper has its own SiteStatusResponse and /backend-api/aura/site_status client.
verevonRelevance: A deterministic reputation/denylist lookup (Quarry already has blocklists in control) before navigation is cheap; decide explicitly whether it fails open or closed and report 'unavailable' distinctly.
notes: Observed fail-open in the service path versus fail-closed in the native helper (see separate record) is an inconsistency worth noting.

name: Navigation scheme policy (http/https/about:blank only)
what: The agent can navigate only to http(s) pages and about:blank; invalid URLs, file:, data:, javascript:, blob: and browser-error pages are refused with a specific message.
how: hS(url) allows j4={about:blank} or protocol in Lg=[http:, https:]; JV() audits outcome 'navigation_url_policy_blocked' with urlSchemeCategory (browser_error, about, blob, data, file, javascript, other, invalid) and throws Ps. Applied in ensureUrlPolicyAllowed for every gated command.
verevonRelevance: Mirror the scheme allowlist in Quarry's navigate/evaluate paths and include the scheme category in denial telemetry.
notes: The plugin description mentions file:// as a local target, but the service policy passes only http/https/about:blank; the main-process restriction separately allows about/blob/data/http/https. Mismatch noted; medium confidence on actual file:// behaviour.

name: Main-process navigation restriction while the agent controls a tab
what: While Browser Use is active, any navigation to a disallowed URL is cancelled by the shell itself, including page-initiated redirects, subframes and window.open, not only agent-initiated goto.
how: Class Wre (browserUseNavigationRestriction) sets threadState.isBrowserUseNavigationRestrictionActive; Gre() returns 'Blocked browser navigation by Browser Use URL policy: <url>' for URLs failing the allowed-scheme test (Zoe allows about/blob/data/http/https). isRestrictedBrowserNavigation is consulted in will-navigate, will-redirect, did-start-navigation, setWindowOpenHandler (deny) and the webRequest onBeforeRequest handler (cancel mainFrame/subFrame). Data and about:srcdoc subframes are exempt; chrome: is allowed only behind a debug flag.
verevonRelevance: Enforcing at the engine layer (not only in the planner or API) is the right model for Quarry's Chromium driver: block redirects, popups and subframe loads by policy in the browser process.

name: Document-response interception with fail-closed request interceptors
what: Main-document responses are paused so that redirects, downloads and response headers can be vetted before the page commits; interceptors that error block the request.
how: class Ff (documentResponses) calls Fetch.enable with pattern {requestStage:'Response', resourceType:'Document'} on every attached tab; handleEvent pauses Document responses, emits 'intercept'/'response' events consumed by the download handling code, and continues or fails them (Fetch.failRequest BlockedByClient). addRequestInterceptor installs priority-ordered request-stage interceptors returning handled | block | continue; an exception is treated as 'block'. Raw CDP cannot use Fetch/Network/Target while interceptors or owned paused responses exist.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's local chromiumoxide driver can adopt a response-stage Document gate to enforce domain grants on redirect targets and to classify downloads before they start.

name: Raw CDP behind three gates plus a method allowlist
what: Raw DevTools Protocol access is off by default, needs per-origin high-risk consent and enterprise permission, and even then only 22 CDP domains (27 listed minus 5 blocked) are reachable, with dangerous methods removed or redirected to safe APIs.
how: Gates: preference full_cdp_access_enabled (default false), per-origin 'full_cdp' allow/deny rules, enterprise featureRequirements.browser_use_full_cdp_access, GaaS requires BROWSER_USE_FULL_CDP_ACCESS_ENABLED; prompt riskLevel 'high' tool_name access_browser_origin_with_raw_cdp. Method policy: domain allowlist ZY (Accessibility, Audits, CacheStorage, Console, CSS, Database, Debugger, DOM, DOMDebugger, DOMSnapshot, Emulation, Fetch, IO, Input, Inspector, Log, Network, Overlay, Page, Performance, Profiler, Runtime, Storage, Target, Tracing, WebAudio, WebAuthn) minus blocked QY {CacheStorage, Database, Storage, Target, WebAuthn}; per-method denylist eZ (e.g. DOM.setFileInputFiles, Input.dispatchKeyEvent, Network.getAllCookies, Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument, Page.setBypassCSP, Page.setDownloadBehavior, Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders, Tracing.requestMemoryDump) with hint text tZ pointing to the safe high-level API; parameter checks nZ (grantUniveralAccess, scriptToEvaluateOnLoad, system tracing). Only the tab's origin is addressable; the docs mark it development-only.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ever exposes CDP to agents (a devtools surface exists in Quarry), copy the deny-by-default posture and per-method allowlist with 'use X instead' hints; otherwise keep CDP internal as today.
notes: The Quarry baseline says the browser UI never sees CDP endpoints; this is consistent.

name: URL-authorising CDP parameters (cookies, requests)
what: CDP calls that carry URLs or cookies must name explicit URLs so each affected origin can be authorised; wildcard or domain-scoped forms are refused.
how: QO map: Network.getCookies requires non-empty urls[] (iZ); Network.setCookie/deleteCookies use d0 (rejects 'domain', sourcePort, sourceScheme; requires 'url'; checks partitionKey.topLevelSite); Network.setCookies uses sZ; Page.deleteCookie requires url; Fetch.continueRequest authorises url; Fetch.fulfillRequest/continueResponse extract Location headers (ZO); Network.getAllCookies, Page.navigate, Network.replayXHR and loadNetworkResource are blocked. Each URL is passed to ensureRawCdpUrlAllowed.
verevonRelevance: Any Quarry cookie-capture or profile feature should scope by explicit URL and run each URL through the same domain authorisation.

name: CDP event buffer with cursors and origin-change purge
what: Agents read page events with a cursor so they can observe exactly what an action caused; events are bounded, filtered by method and target, and dropped when the tab changes origin.
how: rawCdpEventsByTabId ring with per-tab sequence numbers, eviction watermark (truncated flag), readRawCdpEvents({afterSequence, limit 1..1000, methods, target, timeoutMs}); recordRawCdpEvent skips internal screencast events and events during browser-auth protection; discardRawCdpEventsForTab is called when topLevelSecurityOrigin changes. cdp.md documents capture-cursor, act, read-from-cursor.
verevonRelevance: Quarry observations carry console/network summaries; a cursor-based event window per action and purge-on-origin-change would prevent cross-origin leakage between steps.

name: Gated file upload through the file-chooser only
what: Uploads are possible only via the file-chooser event, require per-origin approval (or an enterprise allow) and can be blocked by org policy.
how: file-uploads.md forbids setInputFiles; raw CDP DOM.setFileInputFiles and Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog are denied with redirect hints. ensureCurrentTabFileTransferAllowed('upload') reads the current URL, checks enterprise policy ('uploads' deny => enterprise_policy_blocked), then Zp() prompts 'Allow upload to <url>?' with persist options ['session','always'] when permitted. Settings: upload_approval_mode (always_ask|never_ask) and per-origin uploads rules.
verevonRelevance: Quarry already requires a one-shot approval grant scoped to the exact frame/artifact for upload_ref; add the per-origin persisted option and the enterprise block.

name: Download gating with one-time grants
what: A download proceeds only if it was initiated through an approved agent flow; the approval is a one-time grant tied to the tab, session and exact URL, and it expires.
how: IAB API allowDownload() stores allowedDownloadGrantsByWebContentsId {grantedAtMs, sessionId, url}; consumeAllowedBrowserUseDownload({url, urlChain, webContentsId}) in the will-download handler consumes the grant only when the URL matches; setBlobDownloadOrigin binds blob: downloads to {origin, frameId, tabId, url} after verifying the frame tree origin equals the tab origin. Service side: ensureDownloadAllowed checks scheme policy, enterprise 'downloads' policy, and prompts for the source origin and the current page origin separately ('Allow download from ...?'). download_approval_mode and per-origin downloads rules exist. State machine (download manager): waitForEvent('download') must be armed before the click; an intent installs a request interceptor that follows the first Document request and its redirect chain; a paused Document response classified as a download (Content-Disposition attachment or non-renderable content type) is claimed, security-checked, allowed, then continued; a timeout or error always runs disableDownload which fails any still-paused response (BlockedByClient) and clears blob origin state; blob: downloads must originate from the current website and are only supported on some backends.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's download_ref is driver-gated off; this grant design (URL-bound, single-use, expiring, blob-origin bound) is a ready blueprint to turn it on safely.

name: Cross-origin page-asset fetch approval
what: Bundling a page's images, fonts, stylesheets or videos needs permission for the page origin and for each additional origin the assets come from.
how: pageAssets capability: ensurePageAssetDownloadAllowed (page origin) and ensurePageAssetFallbackFetchAllowed (asset origin differs); both consult enterprise downloads policy and prompt via QR() with tool_params {asset_origins:[origin]}; same-origin fetch is audited as bypassed (policy 'not-cross-origin'). Docs forbid navigating directly to asset URLs to fetch them.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's asset capture (screenshots, images) can reuse the per-origin download policy for third-party hosts.

name: History access approval with bounded queries
what: The agent can read the user's browsing history only after approval, with a small query budget and date bounds, and the approval can be disabled entirely by policy.
how: HR() prompts 'Allow <browser> to use your browsing history for this task?' with an optional persist:'always'. Preference modes history_approval_mode and iab_history_approval_mode in {always_ask, never_ask, disabled}; enterprise requirements.browserUse.allowHistoryAccess=false denies globally (source codex-history-policy). VV() normalises params (queries[], date range, max_results default 100); IAB getUserHistory de-duplicates URLs and caps results.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon browsing-history feature must be ZDR-aware and off by default; adopt the explicit 'disabled' tri-state and query budget.

name: Persistent approvals gated by enterprise policy
what: Users can choose 'never ask' for categories, but admins can forbid global persistent approvals; attempts to persist fail with a clear error.
how: yy(): if approvalMode==='neverAsk' it reads app-server config requirements and throws 'Global persistent Browser Use approvals are disabled by enterprise policy' unless requirements.browserUse.allowGlobalPersistentApproval !== false (kpe). Also checked for history and file-transfer modes (assertBrowserUseGlobalPersistentApprovalAllowed). In the prompt flow, if persistence is not allowed but the UI answers 'always', the answer is rejected (computer-use SDK) or downgraded to conversation scope (browser).
verevonRelevance: Add an org-level 'no persistent approvals' switch to Verevon's approval settings and validate server-side that clients cannot persist more than the policy allows.

name: Browser preferences synced to the server with optimistic concurrency
what: Approval modes and per-origin rules follow the user's account across devices: a local TOML file and a server document are kept in sync, with revision checks and conflict recovery.
how: Local file CODEX_HOME/browser/config.toml (mode 0600, atomic tmp+rename) holds preferences {approval_mode, history_approval_mode, iab_history_approval_mode, download_approval_mode, upload_approval_mode, disable_auto_review, full_cdp_access_enabled, webmcp_enabled(default true)} and rules {origins, downloads, uploads, full_cdp, webmcp -> allowed/denied}. BrowserSettingsSync (class nme) GET/PATCH /wham/browser/settings with expected_revision; 409 triggers re-read; 60 s poll plus fs.watch with 200 ms debounce for two-way sync; a principal (accountId, userId) change clears the local projection; diffs computed by zy(). Defaults: everything 'always_ask', auto-review enabled, full CDP off.
verevonRelevance: Persist per-user approval preferences in the Control Plane (identity/orgs) with revision-based PATCH and let clients mirror them; keep ZDR orgs on ephemeral-only approvals.
notes: The local mirror is plaintext TOML; it contains preference data, no secrets.

name: Structured authorization audit record per decision
what: Each security decision emits a versioned record saying what was decided, by whom (user, automated reviewer, saved permission, network policy, built-in rule, site policy, security mode), why, and how long it took.
how: KN() builds {schema_version:1, permission (browser_auth, browser_history, origin_access, file_upload, file_download, full_cdp, webmcp, page_asset...), decision allowed|denied, decision_context evaluated|not_required|cached|cancelled|error, decided_by (automated_review|user|saved_user_permission|history_policy|network_policy|builtin_rule|openai_site_policy|security_mode), policy, reason, origin (origin only), connector_id, tool_name, backend, duration_ms}. URL-policy and site-status successes are not recorded; only denials. Tables $ee, Hee, Vee map outcomes and sources.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's egress receipts record network facts; an authorisation record with decided_by and decision_context would complete the evidence chain (still ZDR-aware: no durable audit for ZDR orgs).
notes: Origin only, never the full URL, in audit.

name: Signed per-turn verification of 'local browser use enabled'
what: The in-process browser service refuses to act unless the host app proves, per turn, that local browser use is enabled; the proof is a signed response bound to a fresh nonce, session and turn.
how: UF() runs before commands: reads session_id/turn_id from request meta; opens a named pipe from env BROWSER_USE_ACCESS_PIPE_PATH; sends 'browser/access' {executorId, sessionId, turnId, nonce(32 random bytes hex)}; verifies the signature with the SPKI public key in BROWSER_USE_ACCESS_VERIFYING_IDENTITY (node:crypto verify); requires payload === JSON.stringify({domain:'codex.browserAccess.v1', request, allowed:true}); otherwise 'Local browser use is disabled in Work settings'. Cached per (session, turn). 10 s timeout.
verevonRelevance: A signed, nonce-bound capability check between Model Plane and the execution host is a stronger version of BrowserBroker grant revalidation 'before every action'; consider signing grant replies.
notes: Algorithm not named; verify(null, ...) implies an Ed25519-style key (INF).

name: Documentation-read enforcement before risky APIs
what: The agent must have read the confirmation policy document before it may call raw CDP or WebMCP; otherwise the call fails and tells it which doc to read.
how: documents.json marks confirmations with requiredFor: [tab_cdp_call, tab_cdp_events, webmcp_list_tools, webmcp_invoke_tool]. The documentation reader (class _h) records readNames on read()/readBrowser(); assertRequiredDocumentationRead(commandType) throws 'Required documentation has not been read: "confirmations". Read the instructions with await agent.documentation.get("confirmations")'.
verevonRelevance: A cheap, deterministic way to guarantee the planner has the safety policy in context before dangerous actions: gate high-risk Quarry actions on a policy-ack token from the Model Plane session.
notes: Receipts are per runtime session; context compaction resets need cua.rewriteDocumentation().

name: Capability-conditional documentation assembly
what: The documentation the model receives is generated per browser backend and per advertised capability, so it never reads instructions for features that are unavailable.
how: JN() derives disabled API members from api.json 'unsupportedByDefaultIn' plus apiSupportOverrides and env BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_API_MEMBERS; YN() filters documents.json entries by when{browserTypes, requiredApiMembers, requiredBrowserCapabilities, requiredTabCapabilities, excludedTabCapabilities} and modes included | lookup | model; readBrowser() emits '# Selected Browser', included guidance, 'Additional Documentation' lookups and a capability list with per-capability doc commands.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane tool prompts for Quarry actions should be generated from the active driver's capability set (local Chromium vs Browserbase) instead of one static prompt.

name: Per-environment documentation sets
what: Four documentation sets (codex-app, cloud, orbit, training) change safety rules and tab-ownership guidance for the same API depending on where the agent runs.
how: @oai/browser-desktop/environment-docs/{codex-app,cloud,orbit,training}/ each ship api.json, documents.json, browser-safety, confirmations and auth guidance; cua_repl env CUA_REPL_BROWSER_ENV selects the set (default codex-app; cloud and orbit also choose CDP-browser tool descriptions). The training set is shorter (hard 'do not solve CAPTCHAs / bypass paywalls / submit password change').
verevonRelevance: One runtime with several policy profiles (desktop, hosted, training/eval) is the pattern Verevon needs for local vs governed vs eval agent runs.
notes: 'orbit' semantics are not documented; INF: a hosted agent surface similar to cloud.

name: Site-specific instructions injected into page observations
what: After navigation the accessibility header can carry server-supplied per-site guidance that the model should apply but which grants no extra permissions.
how: captureAX/commitCapture prefix: 'Browser tab: <id>, Title: "...", URL: "...", Site Specific Instructions: <json>' when getSiteInstruction(tabId, url) returns text for that exact URL; cloud docs state it comes from OpenAI configuration, must be treated as subordinate to safety rules, and that page title and tree remain untrusted website content.
verevonRelevance: A per-domain 'site playbook' channel (curated hints, known blockers) fed to the planner through the observation would help reliability; mark it trusted-but-non-authorising.

name: Prompt-injection and authorization policy text
what: A concise policy defines what counts as a user instruction, treats all web and tool content as untrusted, and separates reading from transmitting data (typing sensitive data counts as transmission).
how: browser-safety.md and confirmations.md: user-authored text is valid intent; pasted/uploaded/website content is never permission; a sensitive-data list; 'transmitting' includes forms, posts, uploads, WebMCP calls and visiting URLs that embed sensitive data; confirmation must name the exact action, destination and data; vague asks ('do everything in this list') are not blanket approval; group imminent actions but never bundle unclear future steps; do not ask early except before typing sensitive data.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no prompt-injection labelling (known gap); port these definitions into Model Plane system prompts and the approval card copy.
notes: Prompt-level control; enforcement is by the technical gates listed elsewhere.

name: Four-tier confirmation taxonomy
what: Browser actions are classified as hand-off required, always confirm at action time, pre-approval works, or no confirmation; numbered risk classes map to concrete examples.
how: Tier 1 hand-off: final password-change submit, bypassing safety interstitials or paywalls. Tier 2 always confirm: delete data, permissions/account/API keys/saving passwords, CAPTCHAs, install/run software or extensions, representational communication, subscriptions, financial transactions, system settings, medical actions, sensitive-data transmission (must name data and destination; the initial prompt is insufficient). Tier 3 pre-approval works: login (implied by 'go to xyz.com'), permission prompts, age verification, uploads, file management, entering model-generated code. Tier 4 none: cookie banners and ToS during signup, downloads. A parallel Windows variant exists for computer use.
verevonRelevance: Directly usable as Verevon's risk taxonomy for action approval grants; Quarry must not decide approvals, so the Model Plane classifier should own this table.

name: Non-negotiable desktop automation denies
what: Computer use refuses terminals, the Run dialog, the Windows key, password managers, security software, authentication dialogs, age verification and the ChatGPT/Codex apps regardless of confirmation.
how: guidance.md 'Non-negotiable Windows Automation Safety': no Windows terminal via UI automation, no PowerShell or .bat embedded in node_repl, no mixing UIA PowerShell with Computer Use, no Win/Meta/Super/OS key names in press_key, no changing Windows security/privacy settings, no password manager apps or websites; these 'cannot be replaced by confirmation policy'.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ever offers desktop-level agent control, ship an explicit, non-overridable deny list separate from approvals.

name: Secure sign-in handoff (browserAuth)
what: When a site needs credentials the agent never sees them: it describes the visible form, the user types the secrets into a secure host-rendered form, and the runtime fills and submits the page without returning the values.
how: Tab capability 'browserAuth': request({origin, fields[{id,label,type,autocomplete,required,selector}], options[{id,label,selector|field_ids}], submit{selector,action:click|press_enter}, qr_code}) returns only a status {submitted, locator_invalid, page_changed, origin_changed, declined(+reason user_took_over), cancelled, expired, unavailable, submission_failed} plus a non-secret selected_option. Rules: never ask for passwords/OTP in chat, never create accounts, never read or print credential values by any surface, no free-form request text (the client supplies it), one request per sign-in page, unavailable means stop (no fallback to chat or direct entry). Submission diagnostics are a structured event log (prompt_completed, field_fill_*, site_request, site_submission_verified, submit_started...). The prompt is an elicitation with codex_approval_kind 'browser_auth', codex_requires_user_input:true and codex_guardian_compatible:false (an automated reviewer may not answer it), carrying origin, frame_origin, optional cross_origin_iframe, field metadata (accessible_name, autocomplete, input_type, input_name), options, qr_code payload and an optional page screenshot so the user sees what they are signing in to; mobile and unsupported clients get specific error texts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's gap 'no credential vault / no secret-reference action' could be closed with this shape: model supplies selectors and labels, a trusted host collects secrets, Quarry fills in an isolated world and returns only status.
notes: Documented as ChatGPT-hosted secure form; Cloud Browser availability depends on client support (browser_auth_client_unsupported meta).

name: browserAuth request validation (origin, selectors, field heuristics)
what: The runtime refuses credential requests that do not match the live page: wrong origin, selectors that are not unique, visible and enabled, locators from another tab, or fields that look like OTP/new-password where not expected.
how: Schema PDe/FDe/IDe: id regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$ and not __proto__/constructor/prototype; option label 1..120 chars; field_ids max 6; selectors must be strings or PlaywrightLocators bound to the same browser_id and tab_id (OK()). Docs: origin must be scheme+host+port only; options must resolve to exactly one visible enabled element; OTP widgets may target a zero-size autocomplete=one-time-code input. gS() classifies username/password pairs, excluding one-time-code and new-password autocomplete values and OTP/2FA/MFA labels, and only accepts numeric inputs when the label looks like an account number. Result locator_error {field_id, reason:'not_user_visible'}.
verevonRelevance: Strict server-side validation of model-supplied selectors and ids (no prototype keys, bounded lengths, same-tab binding) belongs in any Quarry action that accepts model-provided locators.

name: Native credential delivery in an isolated world
what: Credentials are written into the page by the runtime itself, in a CDP isolated world, so page scripts, the model and tool output never receive the values.
how: browser-auth fill executes evaluateOnPlaywrightSelectorWithTarget(... {operation:'browser-auth-fill', value, nativeSubmitSelector}, {isolatedWorld: nativeDelivery}); values are bounded (GX=16 KiB, XX=50 fields), delivered per field; on failure the status is re-derived through revalidateBeforeAction rather than returning the error text. Raw CDP events are not recorded and raw CDP is refused while credential saving/delivery is protected. In cloud environments a separate browser-auth broker (BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_* env, unix socket) performs 'native' delivery.
verevonRelevance: Quarry can implement 'type secret from vault' as an isolated-world fill that returns {ok} only, and suppress console/network capture for that step.
notes: Broker internals are server-side; only env names and socket path are visible (see broker record).

name: Credential-protection observation gate (state machine)
what: After credentials have been delivered into a document, the agent is blocked from observing that document (AX, DOM, screenshots, retained snapshots) until it navigates to a new document, so typed secrets cannot leak through later observations.
how: Class F0 tracks per-browser state: pending, used, revision, observationRevision, documents (Set of loader ids per tab), permittedDocuments, ordinaryInteractionTabs, manualSavingTabs, usedNativeCredentials. protectDocument() bumps revisions and invalidates documents; assertObservationAllowed() re-reads the loader id before and after each observation and throws credential_observation_restricted | credential_delivery_in_progress | retained_data_restricted when the document is protected, changed mid-observe or retained data is requested; observe() wraps screenshot/AX capture; unknown state sets a poisoned global flag (gh) and every later call fails with credential_state_unavailable. Cloud mode additionally requires ENABLE_BROWSER_SESSION_TAB_OWNERSHIP and the broker socket.
verevonRelevance: A per-document observation lock after secret entry is a design Verevon should adopt for any credential or payment flow: invalidate snapshot refs and redact until the document id changes.
notes: Fail-closed by design: an unknown state blocks all observation for the process lifetime.

name: Machine-readable credential recovery protocol
what: When observation is blocked the error tells the agent exactly what to do next (wait, navigate to a new document, create a new tab, request manual handoff, restart runtime, stop) and a structured meta record is sent to the host.
how: Q4() maps reasons {credential_delivery_in_progress, credential_observation_restricted, retained_data_restricted, credential_state_unavailable, protected_command_failed, browser_security_restricted|unavailable} to text and next_action {retry_after_credential_delivery, navigate_to_new_document, create_new_tab, request_manual_handoff, restart_browser_runtime, retry_after_resolution, stop}; error class Li carries details; XN() emits response meta 'codex/browserCredentialRecovery' {schema_version:1, command, phase, reason, next_action, security_reason, guard_state_before/after, observation_changed, browser_client_version, caas_image_git_commit_sha, credential_binding_version}. Underlying errors are withheld because they may contain protected data.
verevonRelevance: Return a typed 'next_action' with every Quarry refusal so the planner can recover deterministically; withhold raw errors while a protected state is active.

name: Sign-in lifecycle rules (methods, QR, MFA, unknown outcomes)
what: Docs define a complete login flow: list only methods the page offers, let the user choose, never switch methods silently, handle QR and number-matching approvals, treat closed popups as 'unknown', and verify success from a fresh tab.
how: browserAuth.md Authentication Lifecycle: retain target origin before auth; one available method proceeds, several require a user choice via request({options}); QR approval uses request({qr_code:true}) and the runtime decodes the QR (zxing wasm) without exposing the URL; number-matching challenge digits or emoji are read out verbatim; after each transition call getAXState; a closed popup/blank page/timeout is 'unknown'; on failure create a fresh agent tab to the target origin as the first recovery action; report success only on a positive signed-in signal; generic site errors stop after the first occurrence; never tell the user to sign in elsewhere and come back.
verevonRelevance: Good checklist for Verevon's future login handling, especially 'unknown is not failure' and fresh-tab verification.

name: Cloud credential broker bindings
what: Hosted browser sessions fetch credentials from a local broker socket rather than through the model; binding versions are versioned and reported in telemetry.
how: Env/paths seen in the service and main: BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_SOCKET_PATH (must equal /run/codex-browser-auth/browser-auth-broker.sock), BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_CREDENTIAL_BINDING_VERSION in {1,2}, BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_MANUAL_SAVE_BINDING_VERSION in {7,8,10}, ENABLE_BROWSER_SESSION_TAB_OWNERSHIP, gaas.getNativeCredentialObservationStatus(id); the host passes BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_SOCKET_PATH into the node_repl env.
verevonRelevance: Quarry-to-integration-core credential brokering (token vault exists in integration-corev2) could reuse a local-socket broker contract so secrets never traverse the planner.
notes: Broker behaviour is inferred (INF) from env names; server code not present.

name: WebMCP site tools (page-defined agent tools)
what: Pages can register tools through Chromium's document.modelContext; the agent lists them per tab and calls them instead of clicking, subject to per-site settings and review.
how: In-page script (injected via CDP) reads document.modelContext.getTools() filtered to tool.window===window and non-null origin; handles are bound to a registration id (crypto.randomUUID) and a generation counter, exposed as call_name '<tool>__<uuid>'; toolchange events clear handles; stale registrations throw 'WebMCP tool registration is stale. Call fetchTools() again.'; only secure contexts (https, localhost, file) are enumerated and frames are walked including OOPIFs; a probe frame works around a Chromium crash. Settings: webmcp_enabled default true plus per-origin allow/deny lists; resolver results allowed | site-denied | default-denied. Handles expire per turn (docs). webMcpMaxTools default 100 (inventory).
verevonRelevance: If the W3C WebMCP proposal lands, Quarry could prefer site-declared tools over DOM clicking, with the same registration-id and review pattern.
notes: Depends on a Chromium build that exposes document.modelContext (the 'owl' runtime per scout notes).

name: WebMCP activity events to the host UI
what: The host UI receives a compact, size-capped log of WebMCP tool lists and invocations (tool name, title, read-only hint, source hostname, truncated input and output).
how: aF()/iF() build {kind: listTools|invokeTool, name, title, description, readOnlyHint, sourceHostname, inputJson/inputTruncated, outputJson/outputTruncated} within a shared character budget (Qee) and newest-first; host calls setWebMcpToolActivity(toolName, tabId, parentCallId).
verevonRelevance: Pattern for surfacing agent tool activity in the Verevon timeline with bounded payloads.

name: User takeover and interruption signalling
what: If the user takes over the browser (or stops the turn) the agent's runtime errors are summarised naturally and automation stops; secure sign-in returns declined/user_took_over.
how: Constant openai/user_took_over in the service; browserAuth maps an elicitation 'decline' to {status:'declined', reason:'user_took_over'}. Plugin hooks Interrupt, SubagentStop and Stop call node_repl tool turn_ended with {hook_event_name, session_id|agent_id, turn_id}. browser-control-interruption.md tells the agent not to quote raw runtime errors or internal terms. Host state isAgentControllingBrowser / setBrowserUseActive toggle the UI and disable annotation tools while the agent drives.
verevonRelevance: Quarry records control-mode transfer but takeover is advisory server-side; add a hard 'turn ended/interrupted' notification that invalidates in-flight actions and refs.

name: Cloud browser manual handoff
what: For a hosted browser tab the agent can ask the user to take control (for CAPTCHAs, MFA, unusual sign-ins) and the tab is kept alive for the next turn.
how: Tab.requestManualHandoff() maps to command tab_manual_handoff_request, the member is marked unsupported by default on all four backends and the handler requires clientInfo.type==='cdp' plus an advertised tab capability, i.e. the cloud CDP backend switches it on; it marks the tab 'handoff' and the response meta carries cloud_browser_handoff. If the client lacks support the error says not to claim the handoff succeeded. Docs: offer at most once per blocking situation, navigate to the page the user should see first, prefer browserAuth for sign-in, stop before the final step, never offer handoff for implicit account tasks.
verevonRelevance: Quarry live view + takeover exists; add the 'offer once per blocker' rule and a handoff tab mark that preserves the session for the next run.

name: Tab claiming and mention snapshots that fail closed
what: Taking over an existing user tab or a tab mentioned in the prompt requires an exact match of provider tab id, title and URL; otherwise the agent reports it unavailable instead of opening or claiming a different tab.
how: Mentions are plugin://browser@openai-bundled?mention=tab-v1&browserId&tabId&title&url (IAB) or ...source=extension (external) or plugin://chrome@... Resolution: agents.browsers.list() -> match metadata.codexSessionId / extensionInstanceId -> tabs.list()/user.openTabs() -> exact providerTabId+title+url -> claimTab(tab). Claim returns a normal Tab without moving it into an agent tab group; only one session may control a tab (cloud). Ids are never guessed.
verevonRelevance: Use content-addressed tab references (id + title + url snapshot) in Verevon's @tab mention feature to avoid acting on a changed tab.

name: Turn-scoped tab lifecycle with marks
what: Tabs the agent opens are temporary and close when the turn ends unless marked deliverable (stay as output) or handoff (continue next turn); user-opened tabs are untouched.
how: Tab.markDeliverable()/markHandoff() set tab.mark {status, turnId}; IAB turnEnded(): clearSessionBlobDownloads, for each session-controlled tab restorePageClipboards, cleanupDebuggerForTabBestEffort('turn-ended'), then release or keep by mark/lifetime; releaseSessionControl detaches debuggers, clears cursor and active flags. Marks are turn-scoped and the latest wins; cloud doc: deliverable and unmarked user tabs are released at end of turn.
verevonRelevance: Add explicit tab marks to Quarry agent runs so tab/context cleanup at run end is deterministic and ZDR-friendly.

name: Browser management capability with audit trail
what: A guarded capability lets the agent organise windows, tabs, tab groups and bookmarks on user request; every model-initiated change is logged with the pre-change state for undo.
how: browser.capabilities.get('management') exposes Chrome-extension-style windows/tabs/tabGroups/bookmarks proxies (MAIN class bOe, invoke(namespace, method, ...args) over command browser_management_call); getAuditTrail() returns recent changes with {before: bookmarks, tabLayout, windows}. Rules: only requested changes; no navigation, history or page scripting; shared tab groups untouched; http/https bookmark URLs only; explicit confirmation immediately before destructive actions even if pre-authorised; windows non-incognito only.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon builds tab/workspace organisation tools for the agent, copy the before-state audit trail and the destructive-action reconfirmation.

name: Capability registry with documentation-on-demand
what: Optional abilities (browserAuth, pageAssets, webmcp, cdp, botDetection for tabs; management, visibility, viewport for browsers) are advertised per backend and documented only when requested.
how: Registries fOe/TOe map ids to factories; info {id, description}; tab capabilities list: browserAuth, pageAssets, webmcp (only when webMcp enabled); browser capabilities: visibility, viewport (and management). Agent flow: capabilities.list() -> (await capabilities.get(id)).documentation(). Env switches BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_BROWSER_CAPABILITIES / DISABLE_TAB_CAPABILITIES can disable any id.
verevonRelevance: A capability registry is a clean extension point for Quarry agent features (vault fill, asset bundling, takeover) with per-driver availability and env-level kill switches.

name: Backend matrix via unsupportedByDefaultIn
what: One API schema serves four backends (iab, extension, cdp, mcpapps); each member lists the backends where it is off by default and hosts can override.
how: api.json members carry unsupportedByDefaultIn arrays; examples: Browser.user and Browser.history unsupported on iab/cdp/mcpapps; Tabs.content unsupported on iab/extension/cdp/mcpapps; Tab.ax unsupported by default on iab/extension/cdp/mcpapps (re-enabled by the tinysky switch); CUAAPI.downloadMedia off on iab; Tab.requestManualHandoff only on cloud cdp. IAB getInfo returns apiSupportOverrides {Browser.user:false, Browser.history: flag, Tab.markDeliverable:true, Tab.markHandoff:true}. JN() computes the disabled set at runtime.
verevonRelevance: Publish a driver-capability matrix for Quarry drivers (local Chromium, Browserbase, Browserless, Kernel) and generate docs/prompts from it.
notes: api.json lists Tab.ax as unsupported on iab/extension/cdp/mcpapps by default; zte() in the service re-enables it per backend through the 'tinysky' switch (see the AX-mode record), so the AX docs apply only when that mode is on.

name: Playwright-compatible semantic locators with read-only evaluate
what: Agents can drive pages with familiar getByRole/getByText/getByLabel/locator chains, waits and file-chooser events; evaluate runs in a read-only page scope.
how: PlaywrightAPI: domSnapshot, elementInfo (metadata at screenshot coordinates), elementScreenshot (viewport annotated with element bounds and probe point), evaluate (read-only scope), expectNavigation, frameLocator, getBy*, locator, waitForEvent(download|filechooser), waitForLoadState, waitForURL, waitForTimeout. PlaywrightLocator adds click, fill, press, pressSequentially, selectOption, check/uncheck, waitFor, allTextContents, innerText, evaluateAll. Locator actions use shared actionability checks and retry with timing stats. The service injects Playwright's injected-script runtime into each frame/target (ensurePlaywrightInjectedInTarget) rather than driving a Playwright server, so selector semantics match Playwright while all calls stay on the gated CDP channel.
verevonRelevance: Quarry already has semantic locators; confirm 'evaluate' is read-only or approval-gated (known gap: evaluate currently needs no approval).

name: Accessibility-first control with index targets and tree diffing
what: The agent reads a numbered accessibility tree, acts by element index, and receives only a diff of the tree after each batch of actions to save tokens.
how: tab.ax.write() emits the AX state (header with tab id, title, URL) and by default a diff against the previous revision (removed/added/changed); disableDiffing forces full. AX actions: click, drag, paste, pressKey (xdotool-style keys, holds up to 30 s), scroll, selectText (prefix/suffix/selectionType), setValue, typeText, performSecondaryAction (names come from the tree, never guessed). Guidance: batch actions plus one ax.write per REPL call; runtime auto-waits before capturing; if no change reported do not repeat blindly. A WASM engine (browser-accessibility.wasm.br, 4 MB) builds revisions (accessibilityCore.buildRevision, mode auto|full).
verevonRelevance: Quarry snapshots use @eN refs; adding revision-diffed observations would cut Model Plane token cost per step.
notes: Diff text format is produced inside the WASM and not read.

name: Model-visible vs programmatic observation channels
what: Observations are explicit: write/emit calls put state in front of the model, while get calls return data to the script without showing it, so scripts can process page data without leaking it to the model.
how: AXAPI.write(mode) displays state/screenshot/both to the model; AXAPI.get(mode) returns strings/bytes only; nodeRepl.write(value) and nodeRepl.emitImage(image) append to the tool result; documentation and initial UI state are auto-emitted on first selection; tool output is capped (cua_repl js output_token_limit 25000; code-mode exec default max_output_tokens 10000). Credential flows rely on this split (values never reach write()).
verevonRelevance: Quarry's /step returns the full observation to the planner; offering script-side processing channels (extract without echo) would help privacy-sensitive flows under ZDR.

name: Stale target protection (document key and AX revision)
what: Element indexes and DOM ids are valid only for the observation that produced them; actions on stale ids fail loudly and captures that straddle a navigation are discarded.
how: captureCandidate/commitCapture key each capture by documentKey = wr(mainFrameId, loaderId) and accessibilityRevision; commitCapture drops results if the document changed during capture or the session state was replaced (pa error); captureProvenance WeakMap ties output to {sessionId, documentKey, state}; click targets re-resolve with 'Accessibility element N is stale or missing' / 'DOM node N is stale or missing' / 'Click target is no longer available' (frame variants). Windows computer use uses screenshot ids and element indexes valid only for the latest get_window_state.
verevonRelevance: Matches Quarry's TARGET_REPAIR_REQUIRED design; the loader-id keyed discard of in-flight captures is an extra race guard to copy.

name: Hit-tested clicks with scroll, settle and covered-element errors
what: Before clicking an AX element the runtime verifies that the point actually hits the target (including inside nested and cross-process iframes), scrolls it into view, waits for position stability and reports what covers it.
how: s0() computes content quads, then runs elementFromPoint-style probes through each frame hop (DOM.getBoxModel/getContentQuads + coordinate transforms) returning hittable | covered(hitTag) | unpositioned; HO() scrolls via DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded, polls until two consecutive samples match within tolerance, else throws 'Accessibility element N is covered by <tag> or otherwise not hittable' or 'did not settle after scrolling'; unpositioned nodes give 'couldn't be clicked. Try another element'.
verevonRelevance: Port to Quarry's atomic verify-and-act: include covering element tag and settle checks in the ActionOutcome for better planner recovery.

name: AX capture across frames and processes with deadlines
what: The accessibility snapshot merges the main frame, same-process iframes and out-of-process iframes into one tree and reports per-frame failures as warnings instead of failing the whole read.
how: captureAX: Page.getFrameTree + DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot({computedStyles:[], includePaintOrder:false, includeDOMRects:false}) + Accessibility.getFullAXTree per frame; captureSessions walks IFRAME/FRAME nodes, DOM.describeNode -> frameId -> targetForFrameOrAttach, validates parent frame ownership, enables accessibility on the child target, with an overall traversal deadline (XY) and warnings 'Iframe <id> accessibility unavailable: ...'. Each AX node maps to backendDOMNodeId, frame, target and action descriptions (Expand/Collapse).
verevonRelevance: Quarry's snapshot already carries frames[]; add per-frame warnings and a global traversal deadline.

name: Settle heuristics after actions
what: The runtime waits for navigation commit, first paint and AX quiescence with hard caps instead of fixed sleeps, so the model rarely needs explicit waits.
how: Loops in the service: wait for commit/load up to 5 s polling 10 ms; waitForFirstPaint up to 5 s; waitForAXQuiet requires 50 ms (100 ms otherwise) since the last AX update with a 750 ms cap; probeNavigationState evaluates readyState/element count/text length; pending JavaScript dialogs short-circuit waits. Docs say 'It is usually not necessary to pause or delay'.
verevonRelevance: Quarry could standardise settle budgets per action type and expose them in telemetry.

name: JavaScript dialogs exposed as controllable AX nodes
what: alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload dialogs appear in the AX tree with accept/dismiss/prompt controls and screenshots are declined with guidance while a dialog is open.
how: captureJavaScriptDialog builds synthetic nodes via LO(tab, dialog) with dialogTarget {dialogID, control: accept|dismiss|prompt}; screenshot returns screenshot_unavailable 'Screenshot unavailable while a JavaScript <type> dialog is open. Use tab.ax.get("state") and tab.ax.click(elementIndex)'; api.json defines AlertDialog/ConfirmDialog/PromptDialog/BeforeUnloadDialog and Tab.getJsDialog().
verevonRelevance: Quarry has respond_dialog and open dialogs in observations; the 'dialog as AX node' trick unifies the action model.

name: Three input paths: AX, DOM-node CUA, coordinate CUA
what: The same page can be driven by AX indexes, by visible-DOM node ids, or by raw viewport coordinates; guidance says prefer semantic paths and not to jump to coordinates when an action has no effect.
how: CUAAPI (coordinate): click, double_click, drag, keypress, move, scroll, type, downloadMedia. DomCUAAPI: get_visible_dom() (filtered DOM with node ids for interactables), click/double_click/scroll by node_id, type, keypress, downloadMedia. AXAPI as above. api-use-behavior.md: inspect state for blockers before retrying; prefer a fresh DOM snapshot for locator ground truth and a screenshot only for visual confirmation, 'avoid requesting both by default'.
verevonRelevance: Confirms Verevon's mix (refs, click_point, semantic locators); the 'cheapest state check that answers the next question' rule is a good planner prompt line.

name: Screenshot pipeline (JPEG, css/device pixels, fresh screencast frames)
what: Screenshots are JPEG at quality 80, taken in CSS or device pixels, can be clipped or full-page, and are credential-gated.
how: Qk/fG: options {format:Fr(jpeg), quality:80}; css mode scales by 1/devicePixelRatio; device mode tries a short screencast capture (hG): Page.startScreencast, wait up to 2 s for a frame whose metadata timestamp is >= request time (stale frames are acked and ignored), then stopScreencast; fallback Page.captureScreenshot with clip and captureBeyondViewport (5 s cap, 2 s for device viewport). Full page uses Page.getLayoutMetrics cssContentSize. Wrapped in credentialObservationGate.observe.
verevonRelevance: The screencast-freshness trick matters for hidden/background pages (also used by Quarry's frames/stream); check Quarry's screenshot path for stale-frame risk.

name: Virtual clipboard per browser session with restore
what: Paste and copy use a per-session virtual clipboard rather than the OS clipboard, and the page clipboard is restored when the turn ends.
how: TabClipboardAPI read/readText/write/writeText; AXAPI.paste uses 'the browser session's virtual clipboard'; IAB restorePageClipboards() runs in turnEnded and session-activity-ended; internal 'virtual cut' pending state errors ('Browser Use virtual cut is no longer pending').
verevonRelevance: Agent paste should never touch the user's real clipboard; keep that rule for any Verevon desktop shell.

name: Agent cursor with arrival wait
what: The agent's cursor is rendered in the page and actions wait (up to 1.5 s) until the cursor animation arrives before clicking, so users can follow what the agent does.
how: IAB moveMouse(): nextCursorMoveSequence, setBrowserUseCursor({moveSequence, sessionConversationId, x, y}) on hosts; waitForCursorArrival resolves on notifyCursorArrived; cursorArrivalTimeoutMs default 1500; cursor cleared in releaseSessionControl. Related UI: cuaPIP, computerUseOverlay, sendCursorPointToAvatarOverlay (inventory).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's live view could render the agent cursor with arrival acknowledgement to make takeover decisions easier.

name: Approval prompt contract (risk level, persistence options, display params)
what: All approvals use one prompt schema: message, persistence options (session/always), risk level, optional subtitle, and display-friendly parameters.
how: Elicitation meta fields: codex_approval_kind 'mcp_tool_call', codex_request_type 'approval_request' (reviewer-eligible), connector_id ('browser-use' or 'computer-use'), connector_name, persist ('always' | ['session','always'] | ['session']), riskLevel (low|high), subtitle (warning), tool_name, tool_title, tool_description, tool_params, tool_params_display [{name, display_name, value}], tool_call_id, origin, page_url. Computer-use apps: 'Allow Codex to use <App>?'; audio: 'Allow Computer Use to record computer audio?' (never persistent, high risk).

Cloud docs add: information lookups use web search, not Browser; plugin failure never justifies opening the provider site; never probe for a signed-in session; explicit site intent examples; one named-site interaction stays on that site.

name: Plugin mention deep links

name: TinySky mode: accessibility-index control replaces coordinate and DOM CUA
what: A feature-switched mode turns on the accessibility-tree API (numbered elements, diffed state) and turns off the older coordinate-CUA and DOM-CUA input APIs for that backend.

When on it sets apiSupportOverrides {Tab.ax:true, Tab.cua:false, Tab.dom_cua:false}. The desktop host passes the flag to node_repl as BROWSER_USE_TINYSKY_ENABLED and gates the unified computer-use plugin on browserUseTinysky. The same cua API is used in RL training (TinySky).

name: Unified cua API over native apps and browsers
what: One JavaScript API selects apps, windows, browsers and tabs and exposes the same observe/act surface (AX state, screenshot, click by index or point, drag, scroll, selectText, setValue, secondary actions) on all of them.
how: cua.initialize/getState (inventory of apps and browsers), getApp({windowId}|name|bundle), listApps/listWindows, getBrowser, createBrowserTab(browserId,url,{visible,sessionName}), getTab(id | {mention} | {url}), listTabs; Target interface getAXState/getScreenshot/getAXStateAndScreenshot/click/drag/scroll/selectText/setValue/performSecondaryAction; App adds paste/pressKey/typeText; Tab adds goto/back/forward/reload/close/markDeliverable/markHandoff. Stale or ambiguous tab references fail without opening a replacement tab; URL lookups require one exact match; native input wrappers throw on DOM-only tabs (MCP apps).
verevonRelevance: Verevon could expose one agent-facing target abstraction (tab, window, app) behind BrowserBroker so planners don't need per-surface tools.

Launcher env: CUA_REPL_NODE_REPL_PATH, CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES (required: browser | computer | browser,computer; unknown fails startup), CUA_REPL_BROWSER_ENV (codex-app | training | cloud | orbit), NODE_REPL_JS_BANNER. what: The first call must be exactly one entry-point call so its documentation and initial UI state are returned; after a context summary the agent calls rewriteDocumentation() to restore the instructions.

Browser SKILL: read documentation() output in one go, never slice or summarise it; 'Once you have read a browser's complete documentation, do not read it again unless you select a different browser'.

name: Code mode: the model writes JavaScript that orchestrates tools
what: Instead of one tool call per action, the model submits a small JavaScript program that runs in a sandboxed isolate and calls nested tools (including browser/computer-use MCP tools) as async functions.
how: Rust core exec tool: 'Run JavaScript code to orchestrate/compose tool calls'; fresh V8 isolate per exec as an async module, no Node, no filesystem, no network, no console; nested tools on global tools.* with normalised identifiers (tools.mcp__server__tool); helpers text(), image(url|item, detail auto|low|high|original), exit(); first-line pragma // @exec: {"yield_time_ms":N,"max_output_tokens":N} (defaults 10000 tokens); isolate ends when evaluated and unawaited promises are discarded. Config CodeModeConfigToml (default_exec_yield_time_ms, tool_input_schema_max_bytes, excluded_tool_namespaces, direct_only_tool_namespaces); a separate codex-code-mode-host process (74 MB) speaks HostHello/ExecutionStarted/DelegateRequest::InvokeTool messages. name: node_repl host hardening and configuration injection
what: The desktop app launches the Node REPL used for browser/computer use with a curated environment, and writes its MCP server config into Codex core through the app-server so the model cannot alter it from the shell.

Config is pushed with config/batchWrite on keyPath mcp_servers.node_repl and the shell_environment_policy.set entries for NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_CODE_PATHS and the backends var are cleared. Paths resolve through bundled runtime or explicit env override; WindowsApps paths are relocated; node binary and node_repl.exe are cua-built (Node 24.21.0-cua.1).
